heading: File names follow the class
body:
Every class file is named after its one class, as in Java. The file name without the extension is the class name, with the same spelling and the same capital letters, both in client/ and in server/. Rust is the one exception: a Rust file may also use the snake_case form of the name, so `http_reader_service.rs` and `HTTPReaderService.rs` both hold `HTTPReaderService` (ADR 0067). The class name still decides the role and the injection name, and a snake_case file and a PascalCase file with the same class are duplicates. Some examples: `client/services/CartService.ts` holds `CartService`, `server/models/Order.py` holds `Order`, `server/models/Order.rb` holds `Order = Data.define(...)`, and `client/tests/CartServiceTest.go` holds `type CartServiceTest struct`. It covers role files, models, test units, test setups, utilities, error types and every other file in client/ or server/ that declares a class, a struct, a record or another type. A models file holds one model, and it is named after that model. A models file with a second model, for example `Order.ts` with `Order` and `Status`, also fails with `TY1318`. Some files keep the name that Tachyon gives them: views and component files (`tac.html` and its `tac.*` companions) in client/pages/ and client/components/, plain code in client/shared/ and server/shared/, workers in server/workers/ (their class is `Handler`), and the root `middleware.<ext>` file (its class is `Middleware`). A file that declares no type, such as a Python script with functions only, has no class to follow.

Next to its one class and its imports, a file may hold a few lines that run no code: a shebang line and a `"use strict";` line at the top in JavaScript and TypeScript, a module docstring at the top in Python, `declare(strict_types=1);` in PHP, a `package` line in Java and Kotlin, one `namespace` and `#nullable` lines in C#, a `library;` line in Dart, and inner attributes such as `#![allow(dead_code)]` in Rust. A Rust file may also gate an import with `#[cfg(...)]` or `#[cfg_attr(...)]` lines directly above `use`, for example `#[cfg(unix)]` above `use std::os::unix::net::UnixStream;`. A `cfg` line above any other top-level item fails with `TY1310`: put platform code inside the class and gate it there. Code that runs when the file loads fails with `TY1310`: a JavaScript or TypeScript `static { ... }` block, a base class that is computed, such as `extends mixin(Base)`, and a decorator argument that calls or builds something, such as `@Cacheable(options())` (ADR 0044).

A file with another name fails with `TY1318` before the app runs. The message names both fixes: rename the file after the class, or rename the class after the file. `ty migrate fix --write` renames the file when it declares exactly one type. It splits a models file with several models into one file per model: each new file keeps the imports and the comments of its model, and the files that import a moved TypeScript or Dart model import it from its new file. When other files use the old file name, for example in a relay command, it renames the class instead, or lists a manual step (ADR 0067).
